It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, and under the Modern Shrine Ranking System its former Rank was that of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}. The shrine emblem is “double tortoise shell with round, tubular, and comma-shaped jewels” (二重亀甲に丸玉管玉勾玉). == Deities == The deities enshrined are the following four kamiShrine History Document.: :* {{ill|Kushiakarutama-no-kami|ja|櫛明玉神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiakarutama-no-kami|qq=}} (also known as Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto, 櫛明玉命, くしあかるたまのみこと{{Open Access}}[{{NDLDC|1909346/675}} ‘Kokutai Jingido Dictionary’ by Ogura Kōji (Nishikishōdō, 1940) p.1197 – National Diet Library Digital Collection] (accessed February 4, 2018)) :* {{ill|Okuninushi|ja|大国主|lt=Ominamochi|lt_ja=大名持神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okuninushi|qq=}} :* {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|スクナビコナ|1=Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona|lt_ja=少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}} :* {{ill|Ito-take-no-kami|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ito-take-no-kami|qq=}} In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927), one establishment is recorded for Tamatsukuriyu Shrine and one for the shrine known as {{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}}—a total of two. These are respectively identified with the “Tamatsukuri-yusha” and “Yūsha” noted in the [[Izumo Province Fudoki]] (possibly established in the 5th year of Tenpyō (733)). === About the Deities === [[File:140427 Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park Matsue Shimane pref Japan08bs3.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park|ja|出雲玉作史跡公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park|qq=}}}}]] [[File:Tamatsukuri Onsen Panoramic view.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|lt=Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Town|lt_ja=玉造温泉街|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}}}}]] Regarding the kami “Tamatsukuriyu no Kami”, its dual nature as both the “jewel-making deity” and the “hot spring deity” has been noted{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. The former “Tamatsukuri” refers to the crafting of jewels (such as magatama, tubular jewels, and round jewels){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Division (Ancient History)|2006}}. The area around Mount Hanasen, where the shrine is situated, is considered the center of jewel production in the Izumo region; in addition to a dense distribution of Tamatsukuri archaeological sites (the national [[Historic Site]] {{ill|Izumo Tamatsukuri Site|ja|出雲玉作跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri Site|qq=}}) dating from the late [[Yayoi period]],{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}} some of the excavated artifacts are housed at the shrine and have been designated as national [[Important Cultural Property]]{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Furthermore, since the surrounding area is identified with “Kimibe no Kodo” as described in the [[Izumo Province Fudoki]], it is speculated that Tamatsukuriyu Shrine was enshrined by the Tamatsukuri Division—responsible for jewel production under the oversight of the {{ill|Kimibe Clan|ja|忌部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kimibe Clan|qq=}} (Saibe clan){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. In the [[Kogo Shūi]], Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto is recorded as the progenitor of Tamatsukuri in Izumo Province, and the present shrine enshrines him as one of its deities{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. The same work also relates that when {{ill|Ame-no-Totomi|ja|天富命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Totomi|qq=}} led the Saibe clan in the creation of various sacred treasures, he caused the descendants of Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto to produce “Mihokitama” and that his progeny in Izumo Province annually offered jewels along with seasonal produce{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}[[菅田正昭]], Modern Translation of Kogo Shūi (New Person Series 327), Chuokei Publishing, 2014, pp. 92–93.; indeed, in the provisional festival of the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}, it is stipulated that every October the local Tamatsukuri clan of the Iiu District in Izumo Province offers jewels{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Division (Ancient History)|2006}}. The latter aspect, “Onsen deity”, is related to the veneration of {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}} as a divine hot spring. With regard to the deities {{ill|Okuninushi|ja|大国主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okuninushi|qq=}} (also known as Ominamochi) and {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|スクナビコナ|1=Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona|lt_ja=少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}, a theory exists—based on traditions connected with [[Dogo Onsen]] found in a lost passage of the [[Iyo Province Fudoki]]—that these two were enshrined locally as deities of hot springs{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. Furthermore, the remaining deity, {{ill|Ito-take-no-kami|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ito-take-no-kami|qq=}}, is regarded as the deity of the {{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}} recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. This shrine—unique in that six such shrines appear in the record for Izumo Province alone—and bearing the name “Kankoku” (Korea) is speculated to represent a deity invited from the Korean Peninsula{{Sfn|The same, Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}. == History == === Overview === The founding of the shrine is unknown. In the [[Izumo Province Fudoki]] (possibly compiled in the 5th year of [[Tenpyō|Tenpyō]] (733)), the Iiu District entry mentions both “Tamatsukuriyu-sha” and “Yūsha”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}} (the latter perhaps meaning “Hot Spring Shrine”{{Sfn|The same, Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}). In the [[Rikkokushi|National Histories]], it is recorded that in the 1st year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承元|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan|qq=}} (859) on July 11, the Rank of “Yuzashikyo Hime” was elevated from no Rank to lower 5th Rank (as noted in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yuzashikyo Hime”. Then, on November 10 in the 13th year of {{ill|Jōgane|ja|貞観|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgane|qq=}} (871), the Rank of “Yunshin” was raised from upper 5th Rank to lower 4th Rank (also recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}). In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}} (compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927)){{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, entries for “Tamatsukuriyu Shrine” and “{{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}}” appear in Iiu District, Izumo Province, with both classified as {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. In the medieval period, according to the “Shrine History Document” in the ''Kimibe Sōsha Jingūji Nemoto-rokku'', in the 4th year of {{ill|Kenchō|ja|建長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenchō|qq=}} (1252) there is an account of a donation of 5 koku of rice from {{ill|Sasaki Yasutsune|ja|佐々木泰清|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Yasutsune|qq=}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Furthermore, in the 1st year of {{ill|Eiroku|ja|Eiroku|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiroku|qq=}} (1558), a building plaque refers to the shrine as “Yuhime Daimyōjin”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. During the Edo period, the shrine received veneration from the {{ill|Matsue Domain|ja|松江藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue Domain|qq=}}, and besides the establishment of an adjacent tea house, successive feudal lords made pilgrimages and sent deputations{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Notably, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōwa|qq=}} (1803), the 7th daimyō, {{ill|Matsudaira Harukiyo|ja|松平治郷|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Harukiyo|qq=}}, donated a plaque inscribed with “Konan Tamatsukuri Yaku-sen Shrine”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Contemporary documents also refer to the shrine by names such as “Yubune Myōjin” or “Yubune Daimyōjin”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Later, in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857), the current main hall was rebuilt{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji Restoration|qq=}}, the shrine’s name was restored to “Tamatsukuriyu Shrine”, and under the Modern Shrine Ranking System it was initially classified as a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|qq=}}, later being elevated to a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} in March of the 3rd year of {{ill|Showa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Showa|qq=}} (1928){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}. === Kami Ranks === * In the 1st year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承元|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan|qq=}} (859) on July 11, the Rank of “Yuzashikyo Hime” was raised from no Rank to lower 5th Rank (as recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yuzashikyo Hime”. * In the 13th year of {{ill|Jōgane|ja|貞観|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgane|qq=}} (871) on November 10, the Rank of “Yunshin” was raised from upper 5th Rank to lower 4th Rank (also recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yunshin”. == Shrine Facilities == [[File:Tamatsukuriyu jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall (本殿)}}]] * First Torii Gate – The plaque ({{ill|Plaque|ja|扁額|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Plaque|qq=}}) was calligraphed by the 25th/28th {{ill|Prime Minister of Japan|ja|内閣総理大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prime Minister of Japan|qq=}}, {{ill|Wakatsuki Reijiro|ja|若槻禮次郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakatsuki Reijiro|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * Second Torii Gate * Shrine Office * Storage for Excavated Izumo Tamatsukuri Artifacts – Located beside the stone steps along the approach, this storage facility (built in 1960 [Showa 35]) is modeled on ancient house-style haniwa. It houses approximately 700 items related to ancient jewel crafting, including 184 items of jewels and unfinished products, and 162 items (including remnants of grinding stones), which have been designated as national [[Important Cultural Property]]sAccording to the on-site information board.. * Haiden and Main Hall – The main hall was rebuilt in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857) in a modified {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisha-zukuri|qq=}} style{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. * Sacred Water and Wishing Stone – At the shrine office, one receives a “kanaiishi” (wishing stone) and pours the sacred water over both the wishing stone and the kanaiishi; then, by gently touching the wishing stone while silently praying your wish three times, you return to the office to write your wish on an ema. One copy is placed in the plaque holder and the other, along with the kanaiishi, into an amulet bag – thus your wish is said to be grantedAccording to the on-site information board.. * Every January 1st and 2nd, from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, free New Year’s offerings are provided, including crab soup, sweet red bean soup, roasted sweet potatoes, and other dishes. * Shintama Pond * Sesshu-sha – (see below) * {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Yougai Yamashiro|ja|玉造要害山城|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Yougai Yamashiro|qq=}} – The ruins of a mountain castle built on a hill behind the shrine precincts. Remains of earthen ramparts, a dry moat, and well sites are well preservedAccording to the on-site information board.. File:Hengaku of the first torii gate of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Plaque of the First Torii Gate (一の鳥居扁額) File:The second Torii gate of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Second Torii Gate (二の鳥居) File:Cultural Property Storage House of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Izumo Tamatsukuri Artifacts Storage (出雲玉作跡出土品収蔵庫) File:Honden (the main shrine) of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Main Hall as seen from behind (後方より見た本殿) File:Sacred water and sacred stones of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Sacred Water and Wishing Stone (御神水と願い石) File:Matamagaike（pond） of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Shintama Pond (真玉ケ池) == Sesshu-sha == * {{ill|Yuhime Daimyōjin Shrine|ja|湯姫大明神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuhime Daimyōjin Shrine|qq=}} – Deity: Yuhime Daimyōjin. Festival date: {{ill|October 10|ja|10月10日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * {{ill|Kotohira Shrine|ja|金刀比羅神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kotohira Shrine|qq=}} – Deity: {{ill|Ōmononushi|ja|大物主|lt=Ōmononushi-no-mikoto|lt_ja=大物主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=}}. Festival date: {{ill|July 10|ja|7月10日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 10|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * Soga/Kigarashi Shrine (そが・きがらしじんじゃ) – Deity: {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞鳴尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. Festival date: {{ill|March 11|ja|3月11日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/March 11|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * {{ill|Fukutoku Shrine|ja|福徳神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fukutoku Shrine|qq=}} – Deity: {{ill|Okuninushi|ja|大國主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okuninushi|qq=}}. Festival date: {{ill|January 3|ja|1月3日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/January 3|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * {{ill|Sawatama Shrine|ja|澤玉神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sawatama Shrine|qq=}} – Deity: {{ill|Sarutahiko|ja|サルタヒコ|lt=Sarutahiko-no-mikoto|lt_ja=猿田彦命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko|qq=}}. Festival date: {{ill|October 9|ja|10月9日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 9|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * {{ill|Inari Shrine|ja|稲荷神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inari Shrine|qq=}} – Deity: {{ill|Uganomitama-no-mikoto|ja|稲倉魂命|1=Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Uganomitama-no-mikoto|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama|qq=}}. Festival date: {{ill|October 1|ja|10月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 1|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * {{ill|Tamamiya Shrine|ja|玉宮神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamamiya Shrine|qq=}} – Deity: {{ill|Tamamiso-no-mikoto|ja|玉祖命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamamiso-no-mikoto|qq=}}. Festival date: {{ill|September 1|ja|9月1日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/September 1|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * Yuyama Youhaiden – Deity: {{ill|Yuyama-no-omikami|ja|湯山主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yuyama-no-omikami|qq=}} (also known as {{ill|Okuninushi|ja|大国主|lt=Ōmikatakami|lt_ja=大巳貴神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okuninushi|qq=}})According to the on-site information board.. * Fuguya Shrine – An off-site branch of the Shikinaisha “Fuguya Shrine”. File:Yuhime-Daimyou-jinja of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Yuhime Daimyōjin Shrine (湯姫大明神社) File:Kotohira-jinja of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Kotohira Shrine (金刀比羅神社) File:Soga-jinja and Kigarashi-jinja of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Soga Shrine / Kigarashi Shrine (素鵞神社 / 記加羅志神社) File:Fukutoku-jinja of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Fukutoku Shrine (福徳神社) File:Sawatama-jinja of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Sawatama Shrine (澤玉神社) File:Tamanomiya-jinja of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Tamamiya Shrine (玉宮神社) File:Yuyama-Yohaiden of Tamatsukuriyu-jinja.jpg|Yuyama Youhaiden (湯山遥拝殿) == Major Festivals == * Summer Festival ({{ill|July 15|ja|7月15日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/July 15|qq=}}) * Annual Festival ({{ill|October 10|ja|10月10日|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/October 10|qq=}}) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Properties (National Designation) === * Izumo Province Tamatsukuri Excavated Artifacts (archaeological data) – Designated on May 27, Showa 14; additional designation, name change, and item-number revision on February 8, Showa 33{{国指定文化財等データベース|201|9691|Izumo Province 玉作阯出土品}}[http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kunisitei.html National Cultural Properties] (Matsue City website). ** 184 items of jewels and unfinished products ** 162 items including remnants of grinding stones ** 11 glass pieces ** Fragments of crucibles, etc. (grouped) *: These excavated artifacts are stored in the storage facility within the shrine precincts. === National Historic Sites === The shrine precincts have been designated as part of the national historic site “Izumo Tamatsukuri Site” (Miyanoue area), designated on October 12, Taishō 11{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}On-site information board.{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}. === Shimane Prefecture Designated Cultural Properties === * Historic Sites ** Tamatsukuri Tsukiyama Kofun **: A circular tumulus on the western side of the Tamatsukuri area. Excavated in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857), it yielded a bronze mirror, among other items, and presently two boat-shaped stone sarcophagi are exposed“Tamatsukuri Tsukiyama Kofun”, in Japanese Historical Place Names, Volume 33: Place Names of Shimane Prefecture, Heibonsha, 1995.. The tumulus area is part of the shrine grounds. Designated on June 13, Showa 36[http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kensitei.html Prefectural Cultural Properties] (Matsue City website). === Matsue City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Journal of the Upper Bathing Entry (ancient document) – Designated on July 10, Heisei 14[http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/sisitei.html City Designated Cultural Properties] (Matsue City website). ** Excavated Materials from the Tamatsukuri Ancient Tomb (archaeological data) – Designated on March 31, Showa 61. == On-site Information == '''Address''' * {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}{{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}} Tamayu Town Tamatsukuri 508 '''Access''' * From {{ill|West Japan Railway Company (JR West)|ja|西日本旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/West Japan Railway Company (JR West)|qq=}}’s {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Station|ja|玉造温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Station|qq=}} ** Bus: Take {{ill|Ichihata Bus|ja|一畑バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichihata Bus|qq=}} (bound for {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}}) and alight at the “Tamatsukuriyu Onsen” bus stop. Park|ja|出雲玉作史跡公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park|qq=}} * Izumo Tamatsukuri Museum * {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Yougai Yamashiro {{Shrine | Name = Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (玉作湯神社) | image = [[File:Tamatsukuriyu-jinja, haiden.jpg|270px]]
Worship Hall | location = {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}, {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, Tamayu Town, Tamatsukuri 508 | Coordinates = {{Coord|35|24|49.2|N|133|0|42.3|E|display=title,inline}} | Deities = {{ill|Kushiakarutama-no-Kami|ja|櫛明玉神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiakarutama-no-Kami|qq=}}
{{ill|Ōnamuchi-no-Kami|ja|大名持神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōnamuchi-no-Kami|qq=}}
{{ill|Sukunabikona-no-Kami|ja|少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona-no-Kami|qq=}}
{{ill|Itakeru-no-Kami|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Itakeru-no-Kami|qq=}} (auxiliary deity) | Shrine Rank = {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}} (small)
Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} | Established = Unknown | Main hall = Taisha-zukuri style | Annual festival = October 10 | Map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=Tamatsukuriyu Shrine|coordinates={{coord2|35|24|49.2|N|133|0|42.3|E}}|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} }} [[File:Tamatsukuriyu-jinja, torii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii Gate}}]] '''Tamatsukuriyu Shrine''' (玉作湯神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, with its former shrine Rank classified as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}. The shrine crest is a "double tortoise shell with a circular jewel and comma-shaped beads." == Deities == The enshrined deities are the following four: * {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|ja|櫛明玉神|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto=Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|lt=Kushiakarutama-no-Kami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (also known as Kushiakarutama-no-Mikoto) * {{ill|Ōnamuchi-no-Kami|ja|大名持神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōnamuchi-no-Kami|qq=}} * {{ill|Sukunabikona-no-Kami|ja|少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona-no-Kami|qq=}} * {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == The origin of the shrine is unknown. It is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Fudoki|qq=}} as "Tamatsukuri-yu Shrine." The shrine has been supported by various ruling clans over the centuries, including the {{ill|Matsue Domain|ja|松江藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue Domain|qq=}} during the Edo period. The current main hall was rebuilt in 1857 (Ansei 4), following the Taisha-zukuri architectural style. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji Restoration|qq=}}, the shrine was Ranked as a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|qq=}} before being promoted to {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} in 1928 (Shōwa 3). == Grounds == [[File:Tamatsukuriyu jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall}}]] * First Torii Gate - Inscribed by {{ill|Reijirō Wakatsuki|ja|若槻禮次郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Reijirō Wakatsuki|qq=}}, the 25th and 28th Prime Minister of Japan. * Second Torii Gate * Shrine Office * Repository for artifacts excavated from the {{ill|Izumo Tamatsukuri site|ja|出雲玉作跡|lt=Izumo Tamatsukuri Archaeological Site|Izumo Tamatsukuri site=Izumo Tamatsukuri site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri site|qq=}}, designated as an Important Cultural Property of Japan. == Subsidiary Shrines == * Yuhime Daimyōjin Shrine – Enshrines Yuhime Daimyōjin * Kotohira Shrine – Enshrines {{ill|Ōmononushi-no-Kami|ja|大物主命|1=Ōmononushi|lt=Ōmononushi-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmononushi|qq=}} * Soga and Kigarashi Shrines – Enshrines {{ill|Susanoo-no-Mikoto|ja|素盞鳴尊|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Susanoo-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * Fukutoku Shrine – Enshrines {{ill|Ōkuninushi-no-Kami|ja|大國主命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōkuninushi-no-Kami|qq=}} * Sawatama Shrine – Enshrines {{ill|Sarutahiko-no-Ōkami|ja|猿田彦命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko-no-Ōkami|qq=}} * Inari Shrine – Enshrines {{ill|Ukanomitama-no-Kami|ja|稲倉魂命|1=Ukanomitama|lt=Ukanomitama-no-Mikoto|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama-no-Kami|13=User:Immanuelle/Ukanomitama|qq=}} * Tamamiya Shrine – Enshrines {{ill|Tamanoya-no-Mikoto|ja|玉祖命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanoya-no-Mikoto|qq=}} * Yuyama Worship Hall – Enshrines Yuyama-no-Kami == Main Festivals == * Summer Festival (July 15) * Annual Grand Festival (October 10) == Cultural Properties == === Important Cultural Property (National Designation) === * Artifacts excavated from the Izumo Tamatsukuri site, including comma-shaped beads and unfinished products, designated on May 27, 1939. === National Historic Site === * Part of the shrine grounds is designated as the {{ill|Izumo Tamatsukuri site|ja|出雲玉作跡|lt=Izumo Tamatsukuri Archaeological Site|Izumo Tamatsukuri site=Izumo Tamatsukuri site|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri site|qq=}}. == Access == * Located in Tamayu Town, Tamatsukuri 508, {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}. * Accessible via bus from {{ill|Tamatsukuri Onsen Station|ja|玉造温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuri Onsen Station|qq=}} on the {{ill|JR West|ja|西日本旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/JR West|qq=}} line. == It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, and under the Modern Shrine Ranking System its former Rank was that of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}. The shrine emblem is “double tortoise shell with round, tubular, and comma-shaped jewels” (二重亀甲に丸玉管玉勾玉). == Deities == The deities enshrined are the following four kamiShrine History Document.: :* {{ill|Kushiakarutama-no-kami|ja|櫛明玉神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiakarutama-no-kami|qq=}} (also known as Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto, 櫛明玉命, くしあかるたまのみこと{{Open Access}}[{{NDLDC|1909346/675}} ‘Kokutai Jingido Dictionary’ by Ogura Kōji (Nishikishōdō, 1940) p.1197 – National Diet Library Digital Collection] (accessed February 4, 2018)) :* {{ill|Okuninushi|ja|大国主|lt=Ominamochi|lt_ja=大名持神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okuninushi|qq=}} :* {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|スクナビコナ|1=Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona|lt_ja=少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}} :* {{ill|Ito-take-no-kami|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ito-take-no-kami|qq=}} In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927), one establishment is recorded for Tamatsukuriyu Shrine and one for the shrine known as {{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}}—a total of two. These are respectively identified with the “Tamatsukuri-yusha” and “Yūsha” noted in the [[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Izumo Province Fudoki]] (possibly established in the 5th year of Tenpyō (733)). === About the Deities === [[File:140427 Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park Matsue Shimane pref Japan08bs3.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park|ja|出雲玉作史跡公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park|qq=}}}}]] [[File:Tamatsukuri Onsen Panoramic view.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|lt=Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Town|lt_ja=玉造温泉街|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}}}}]] Regarding the kami “Tamatsukuriyu no Kami”, its dual nature as both the “jewel-making deity” and the “hot spring deity” has been noted{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. The former “Tamatsukuri” refers to the crafting of jewels (such as magatama, tubular jewels, and round jewels){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Division (Ancient History)|2006}}. The area around Mount Hanasen, where the shrine is situated, is considered the center of jewel production in the Izumo region; in addition to a dense distribution of Tamatsukuri archaeological sites (the national [[Historic Site]] {{ill|Izumo Tamatsukuri Site|ja|出雲玉作跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri Site|qq=}}) dating from the late [[Yayoi period]],{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}} some of the excavated artifacts are housed at the shrine and have been designated as national [[Important Cultural Property]]{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Furthermore, since the surrounding area is identified with “Kimibe no Kodo” as described in the [[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Izumo Province Fudoki]], it is speculated that Tamatsukuriyu Shrine was enshrined by the Tamatsukuri Division—responsible for jewel production under the oversight of the {{ill|Kimibe Clan|ja|忌部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kimibe Clan|qq=}} (Saibe clan){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. In the [[Kogo Shūi]], Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto is recorded as the progenitor of Tamatsukuri in Izumo Province, and the present shrine enshrines him as one of its deities{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. The same work also relates that when {{ill|Ame-no-Totomi|ja|天富命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Totomi|qq=}} led the Saibe clan in the creation of various sacred treasures, he caused the descendants of Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto to produce “Mihokitama” and that his progeny in Izumo Province annually offered jewels along with seasonal produce{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}[[菅田正昭]], Modern Translation of Kogo Shūi (New Person Series 327), Chuokei Publishing, 2014, pp. 92–93.; indeed, in the provisional festival of the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}, it is stipulated that every October the local Tamatsukuri clan of the Iiu District in Izumo Province offers jewels{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Division (Ancient History)|2006}}. The latter aspect, “Onsen deity”, is related to the veneration of {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}} as a divine hot spring. With regard to the deities {{ill|Okuninushi|ja|大国主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okuninushi|qq=}} (also known as Ominamochi) and {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|スクナビコナ|1=Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona|lt_ja=少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}, a theory exists—based on traditions connected with [[Dogo Onsen]] found in a lost passage of the [[Iyo Province Fudoki]]—that these two were enshrined locally as deities of hot springs{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. Furthermore, the remaining deity, {{ill|Ito-take-no-kami|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ito-take-no-kami|qq=}}, is regarded as the deity of the {{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}} recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. This shrine—unique in that six such shrines appear in the record for Izumo Province alone—and bearing the name “Kankoku” (Korea) is speculated to represent a deity invited from the Korean Peninsula{{Sfn|The same, Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}. == History == === Overview === The founding of the shrine is unknown. In the [[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Izumo Province Fudoki]] (possibly compiled in the 5th year of [[Tenpyō|Tenpyō]] (733)), the Iiu District entry mentions both “Tamatsukuriyu-sha” and “Yūsha”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}} (the latter perhaps meaning “Hot Spring Shrine”{{Sfn|The same, Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}). In the [[Rikkokushi|National Histories]], it is recorded that in the 1st year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承元|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan|qq=}} (859) on July 11, the Rank of “Yuzashikyo Hime” was elevated from no Rank to lower 5th Rank (as noted in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yuzashikyo Hime”. Then, on November 10 in the 13th year of {{ill|Jōgane|ja|貞観|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgane|qq=}} (871), the Rank of “Yunshin” was raised from upper 5th Rank to lower 4th Rank (also recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}). In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}} (compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927)){{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, entries for “Tamatsukuriyu Shrine” and “{{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}}” appear in Iiu District, Izumo Province, with both classified as {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. In the medieval period, according to the “Shrine History Document” in the ''Kimibe Sōsha Jingūji Nemoto-rokku'', in the 4th year of {{ill|Kenchō|ja|建長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenchō|qq=}} (1252) there is an account of a donation of 5 koku of rice from {{ill|Sasaki Yasutsune|ja|佐々木泰清|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Yasutsune|qq=}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Furthermore, in the 1st year of {{ill|Eiroku|ja|Eiroku|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiroku|qq=}} (1558), a building plaque refers to the shrine as “Yuhime Daimyōjin”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. During the Edo period, the shrine received veneration from the {{ill|Matsue Domain|ja|松江藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue Domain|qq=}}, and besides the establishment of an adjacent tea house, successive feudal lords made pilgrimages and sent deputations{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Notably, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōwa|qq=}} (1803), the 7th daimyō, {{ill|Matsudaira Harukiyo|ja|松平治郷|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Harukiyo|qq=}}, donated a plaque inscribed with “Konan Tamatsukuri Yaku-sen Shrine”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Contemporary documents also refer to the shrine by names such as “Yubune Myōjin” or “Yubune Daimyōjin”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Later, in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857), the current main hall was rebuilt{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji Restoration|qq=}}, the shrine’s name was restored to “Tamatsukuriyu Shrine”, and under the Modern Shrine Ranking System it was initially classified as a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|qq=}}, later being elevated to a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} in March of the 3rd year of {{ill|Showa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Showa|qq=}} (1928){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}. === Kami Ranks === * In the 1st year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承元|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan|qq=}} (859) on July 11, the Rank of “Yuzashikyo Hime” was raised from no Rank to lower 5th Rank (as recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yuzashikyo Hime”. * In the 13th year of {{ill|Jōgane|ja|貞観|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgane|qq=}} (871) on November 10, the Rank of “Yunshin” was raised from upper 5th Rank to lower 4th Rank (also recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yunshin”. == Shrine Facilities == [[File:Tamatsukuriyu jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall (本殿)}}]] * First Torii Gate – The plaque ({{ill|Plaque|ja|扁額|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Plaque|qq=}}) was calligraphed by the 25th/28th {{ill|Prime Minister of Japan|ja|内閣総理大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prime Minister of Japan|qq=}}, {{ill|Wakatsuki Reijiro|ja|若槻禮次郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakatsuki Reijiro|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * Second Torii Gate * Shrine Office * Storage for Excavated Izumo Tamatsukuri Artifacts – Located beside the stone steps along the approach, this storage facility (built in 1960 [Showa 35]) is modeled on ancient house-style haniwa. It houses approximately 700 items related to ancient jewel crafting, including 184 items of jewels and unfinished products, and 162 items (including remnants of grinding stones), which have been designated as national [[Important Cultural Property]]sAccording to the on-site information board.. * Haiden and Main Hall – The main hall was rebuilt in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857) in a modified {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisha-zukuri|qq=}} style{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. * Sacred Water and Wishing Stone – At the shrine office, one receives a “kanaiishi” (wishing stone) and pours the sacred water over both the wishing stone and the kanaiishi; then, by gently touching the wishing stone while silently praying your wish three times, you return to the office to write your wish on an ema. One copy is placed in the plaque holder and the other, along with the kanaiishi, into an amulet bag – thus your wish is said to be grantedAccording to the on-site information board.. * Every January 1st and 2nd, from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, free New Year’s offerings are provided, including crab soup, sweet red bean soup, roasted sweet potatoes, and other dishes. * Shintama Pond * Sesshu-sha – (see below) * {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Yougai Yamashiro|ja|玉造要害山城|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Yougai Yamashiro|qq=}} – The ruins of a mountain castle built on a hill behind the shrine precincts. Remains of earthen ramparts, a dry moat, and well sites are well preservedAccording to the on-site information board.. Excavated in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857), it yielded a bronze mirror, among other items, and presently two boat-shaped stone sarcophagi are exposed“Tamatsukuri Tsukiyama Kofun”, in Japanese Historical Place Names, Volume 33: Place Names of Shimane Prefecture, Heibonsha, 1995.. The tumulus area is part of the shrine grounds. Designated on June 13, Showa 36[http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kensitei.html Prefectural Cultural Properties] (Matsue City website). === Matsue City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Journal of the Upper Bathing Entry (ancient document) – Designated on July 10, Heisei 14[http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/sisitei.html City Designated Cultural Properties] (Matsue City website). ** Excavated Materials from the Tamatsukuri Ancient Tomb (archaeological data) – Designated on March 31, Showa 61. == On-site Information == '''Address''' * {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}{{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}} Tamayu Town Tamatsukuri 508 '''Access''' * From {{ill|West Japan Railway Company (JR West)|ja|西日本旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/West Japan Railway Company (JR West)|qq=}}’s {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Station|ja|玉造温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Station|qq=}} ** Bus: Take {{ill|Ichihata Bus|ja|一畑バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichihata Bus|qq=}} (bound for {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}}) and alight at the “Tamatsukuriyu Onsen” bus stop. Former {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} | Established = Unknown | Main hall = Taisha-zukuri style | Annual festival = October 10 | Map = {{location map|Japan Shimane|label=Tamatsukuriyu Shrine|coordinates={{coord2|35|24|49.2|N|133|0|42.3|E}}|position=bottom|width=200|mark=Shinto torii icon vermillion.svg|marksize=15|float=center|caption=}} }} [[File:Tamatsukuriyu-jinja, torii.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|First Torii Gate}}]] '''Tamatsukuriyu Shrine''' (玉作湯神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|ja|神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shinto shrine|qq=}} located in {{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}}, {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, with its former shrine Rank classified as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}. The shrine crest is a "double tortoise shell with a circular jewel and comma-shaped beads." == Deities == The enshrined deities are the following four: * {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|ja|櫛明玉神|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto=Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|lt=Kushiakarutama-no-Kami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (also known as Kushiakarutama-no-Mikoto) * {{ill|Ōnamuchi-no-Kami|ja|大名持神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōnamuchi-no-Kami|qq=}} * {{ill|Sukunabikona-no-Kami|ja|少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona-no-Kami|qq=}} * {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == The origin of the shrine is unknown. It is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Fudoki|qq=}} as "Tamatsukuri-yu Shrine." The shrine has been supported by various ruling clans over the centuries, including the {{ill|Matsue Domain|ja|松江藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue Domain|qq=}} during the Edo period. The current main hall was rebuilt in 1857 (Ansei 4), following the Taisha-zukuri architectural style. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji Restoration|qq=}}, the shrine was Ranked as a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|qq=}} before being promoted to {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} in 1928 (Shōwa 3). == Grounds == [[File:Tamatsukuriyu jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall}}]] * First Torii Gate - Inscribed by {{ill|Reijirō It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, and under the Modern Shrine Ranking System its former Rank was that of a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}. The shrine emblem is “double tortoise shell with round, tubular, and comma-shaped jewels” (二重亀甲に丸玉管玉勾玉). == Deities == The deities enshrined are the following four kamiShrine History Document.: :* {{ill|Kushiakarutama-no-kami|ja|櫛明玉神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kushiakarutama-no-kami|qq=}} (also known as Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto, 櫛明玉命, くしあかるたまのみこと{{Open Access}}[{{NDLDC|1909346/675}} ‘Kokutai Jingido Dictionary’ by Ogura Kōji (Nishikishōdō, 1940) p.1197 – National Diet Library Digital Collection] (accessed February 4, 2018)) :* {{ill|Okuninushi|ja|大国主|lt=Ominamochi|lt_ja=大名持神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okuninushi|qq=}} :* {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|スクナビコナ|1=Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona|lt_ja=少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}} :* {{ill|Ito-take-no-kami|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ito-take-no-kami|qq=}} In the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927), one establishment is recorded for Tamatsukuriyu Shrine and one for the shrine known as {{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}}—a total of two. These are respectively identified with the “Tamatsukuri-yusha” and “Yūsha” noted in the [[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Izumo Province Fudoki]] (possibly established in the 5th year of Tenpyō (733)). === About the Deities === [[File:140427 Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park Matsue Shimane pref Japan08bs3.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park|ja|出雲玉作史跡公園|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri Historical Park|qq=}}}}]] [[File:Tamatsukuri Onsen Panoramic view.JPG|thumb|220px|right|{{center|{{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|lt=Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Town|lt_ja=玉造温泉街|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}}}}]] Regarding the kami “Tamatsukuriyu no Kami”, its dual nature as both the “jewel-making deity” and the “hot spring deity” has been noted{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. The former “Tamatsukuri” refers to the crafting of jewels (such as magatama, tubular jewels, and round jewels){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Division (Ancient History)|2006}}. The area around Mount Hanasen, where the shrine is situated, is considered the center of jewel production in the Izumo region; in addition to a dense distribution of Tamatsukuri archaeological sites (the national [[Historic Site]] {{ill|Izumo Tamatsukuri Site|ja|出雲玉作跡|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Tamatsukuri Site|qq=}}) dating from the late [[Yayoi period]],{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}} some of the excavated artifacts are housed at the shrine and have been designated as national [[Important Cultural Property]]{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Furthermore, since the surrounding area is identified with “Kimibe no Kodo” as described in the [[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Izumo Province Fudoki]], it is speculated that Tamatsukuriyu Shrine was enshrined by the Tamatsukuri Division—responsible for jewel production under the oversight of the {{ill|Kimibe Clan|ja|忌部氏|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kimibe Clan|qq=}} (Saibe clan){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. In the [[Kogo Shūi]], Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto is recorded as the progenitor of Tamatsukuri in Izumo Province, and the present shrine enshrines him as one of its deities{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. The same work also relates that when {{ill|Ame-no-Totomi|ja|天富命|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Totomi|qq=}} led the Saibe clan in the creation of various sacred treasures, he caused the descendants of Kushiakarutama-no-mikoto to produce “Mihokitama” and that his progeny in Izumo Province annually offered jewels along with seasonal produce{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}[[菅田正昭]], Modern Translation of Kogo Shūi (New Person Series 327), Chuokei Publishing, 2014, pp. 92–93.; indeed, in the provisional festival of the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}}, it is stipulated that every October the local Tamatsukuri clan of the Iiu District in Izumo Province offers jewels{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Division (Ancient History)|2006}}. The latter aspect, “Onsen deity”, is related to the veneration of {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}} as a divine hot spring. With regard to the deities {{ill|Okuninushi|ja|大国主|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Okuninushi|qq=}} (also known as Ominamochi) and {{ill|Sukunabikona|ja|スクナビコナ|1=Sukunabikona|lt=Sukunahikona|lt_ja=少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona|qq=}}, a theory exists—based on traditions connected with [[Dogo Onsen]] found in a lost passage of the [[Iyo Province Fudoki]]—that these two were enshrined locally as deities of hot springs{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Deities)|2000}}. Furthermore, the remaining deity, {{ill|Ito-take-no-kami|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ito-take-no-kami|qq=}}, is regarded as the deity of the {{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}} recorded in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}. This shrine—unique in that six such shrines appear in the record for Izumo Province alone—and bearing the name “Kankoku” (Korea) is speculated to represent a deity invited from the Korean Peninsula{{Sfn|The same, Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}. == History == === Overview === The founding of the shrine is unknown. In the [[Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|Izumo Province Fudoki]] (possibly compiled in the 5th year of [[Tenpyō|Tenpyō]] (733)), the Iiu District entry mentions both “Tamatsukuriyu-sha” and “Yūsha”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}} (the latter perhaps meaning “Hot Spring Shrine”{{Sfn|The same, Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}). In the [[Rikkokushi|National Histories]], it is recorded that in the 1st year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承元|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan|qq=}} (859) on July 11, the Rank of “Yuzashikyo Hime” was elevated from no Rank to lower 5th Rank (as noted in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yuzashikyo Hime”. Then, on November 10 in the 13th year of {{ill|Jōgane|ja|貞観|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgane|qq=}} (871), the Rank of “Yunshin” was raised from upper 5th Rank to lower 4th Rank (also recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}). In the {{ill|Engishiki|ja|延喜式|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki|qq=}} (compiled in the 5th year of Enchō (927)){{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|lt=Jinmyōchō|lt_ja=神名帳|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}, entries for “Tamatsukuriyu Shrine” and “{{ill|Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|ja|同社坐韓国伊太氐神社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Zaka-Kankoku Itate Shrine|qq=}}” appear in Iiu District, Izumo Province, with both classified as {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. In the medieval period, according to the “Shrine History Document” in the ''Kimibe Sōsha Jingūji Nemoto-rokku'', in the 4th year of {{ill|Kenchō|ja|建長|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kenchō|qq=}} (1252) there is an account of a donation of 5 koku of rice from {{ill|Sasaki Yasutsune|ja|佐々木泰清|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sasaki Yasutsune|qq=}}{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Furthermore, in the 1st year of {{ill|Eiroku|ja|Eiroku|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Eiroku|qq=}} (1558), a building plaque refers to the shrine as “Yuhime Daimyōjin”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. During the Edo period, the shrine received veneration from the {{ill|Matsue Domain|ja|松江藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue Domain|qq=}}, and besides the establishment of an adjacent tea house, successive feudal lords made pilgrimages and sent deputations{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Notably, in the 3rd year of {{ill|Kyōwa|ja|享和|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kyōwa|qq=}} (1803), the 7th daimyō, {{ill|Matsudaira Harukiyo|ja|松平治郷|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsudaira Harukiyo|qq=}}, donated a plaque inscribed with “Konan Tamatsukuri Yaku-sen Shrine”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Contemporary documents also refer to the shrine by names such as “Yubune Myōjin” or “Yubune Daimyōjin”{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. Later, in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857), the current main hall was rebuilt{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji Restoration|qq=}}, the shrine’s name was restored to “Tamatsukuriyu Shrine”, and under the Modern Shrine Ranking System it was initially classified as a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|qq=}}, later being elevated to a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} in March of the 3rd year of {{ill|Showa|ja|昭和|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Showa|qq=}} (1928){{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Shikinaisha)|1983}}. === Kami Ranks === * In the 1st year of {{ill|Jōgan|ja|承元|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgan|qq=}} (859) on July 11, the Rank of “Yuzashikyo Hime” was raised from no Rank to lower 5th Rank (as recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yuzashikyo Hime”. * In the 13th year of {{ill|Jōgane|ja|貞観|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Jōgane|qq=}} (871) on November 10, the Rank of “Yunshin” was raised from upper 5th Rank to lower 4th Rank (also recorded in the {{ill|Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|ja|日本三代実録|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku|qq=}}) – the inscription reads “Yunshin”. == Shrine Facilities == [[File:Tamatsukuriyu jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall (本殿)}}]] * First Torii Gate – The plaque ({{ill|Plaque|ja|扁額|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Plaque|qq=}}) was calligraphed by the 25th/28th {{ill|Prime Minister of Japan|ja|内閣総理大臣|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prime Minister of Japan|qq=}}, {{ill|Wakatsuki Reijiro|ja|若槻禮次郎|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wakatsuki Reijiro|qq=}}According to the on-site information board.. * Second Torii Gate * Shrine Office * Storage for Excavated Izumo Tamatsukuri Artifacts – Located beside the stone steps along the approach, this storage facility (built in 1960 [Showa 35]) is modeled on ancient house-style haniwa. It houses approximately 700 items related to ancient jewel crafting, including 184 items of jewels and unfinished products, and 162 items (including remnants of grinding stones), which have been designated as national [[Important Cultural Property]]sAccording to the on-site information board.. * Haiden and Main Hall – The main hall was rebuilt in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857) in a modified {{ill|Taisha-zukuri|ja|大社造|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Taisha-zukuri|qq=}} style{{Sfn|Tamatsukuriyu Shrine (Heibonsha)|1995}}. * Sacred Water and Wishing Stone – At the shrine office, one receives a “kanaiishi” (wishing stone) and pours the sacred water over both the wishing stone and the kanaiishi; then, by gently touching the wishing stone while silently praying your wish three times, you return to the office to write your wish on an ema. One copy is placed in the plaque holder and the other, along with the kanaiishi, into an amulet bag – thus your wish is said to be grantedAccording to the on-site information board.. * Every January 1st and 2nd, from 9:00 AM to 4:00 PM, free New Year’s offerings are provided, including crab soup, sweet red bean soup, roasted sweet potatoes, and other dishes. * Shintama Pond * Sesshu-sha – (see below) * {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Yougai Yamashiro|ja|玉造要害山城|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Yougai Yamashiro|qq=}} – The ruins of a mountain castle built on a hill behind the shrine precincts. Remains of earthen ramparts, a dry moat, and well sites are well preservedAccording to the on-site information board.. Excavated in the 4th year of {{ill|Ansei|ja|安政|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ansei|qq=}} (1857), it yielded a bronze mirror, among other items, and presently two boat-shaped stone sarcophagi are exposed“Tamatsukuri Tsukiyama Kofun”, in Japanese Historical Place Names, Volume 33: Place Names of Shimane Prefecture, Heibonsha, 1995.. The tumulus area is part of the shrine grounds. Designated on June 13, Showa 36[http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/kensitei.html Prefectural Cultural Properties] (Matsue City website). === Matsue City Designated Cultural Properties === * Tangible Cultural Properties ** Journal of the Upper Bathing Entry (ancient document) – Designated on July 10, Heisei 14[http://www1.city.matsue.shimane.jp/bunka/bunkazai/siteibun/sisitei.html City Designated Cultural Properties] (Matsue City website). ** Excavated Materials from the Tamatsukuri Ancient Tomb (archaeological data) – Designated on March 31, Showa 61. == On-site Information == '''Address''' * {{ill|Shimane Prefecture|ja|島根県|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shimane Prefecture|qq=}}{{ill|Matsue City|ja|松江市|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue City|qq=}} Tamayu Town Tamatsukuri 508 '''Access''' * From {{ill|West Japan Railway Company (JR West)|ja|西日本旅客鉄道|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/West Japan Railway Company (JR West)|qq=}}’s {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Station|ja|玉造温泉駅|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen Station|qq=}} ** Bus: Take {{ill|Ichihata Bus|ja|一畑バス|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ichihata Bus|qq=}} (bound for {{ill|Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|ja|玉造温泉|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamatsukuriyu Onsen|qq=}}) and alight at the “Tamatsukuriyu Onsen” bus stop. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|qq=draft|1=Shikinaisha|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|qq=}}, with its former shrine Rank classified as a {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}}. The shrine crest is a "double tortoise shell with a circular jewel and comma-shaped beads." == Deities == The enshrined deities are the following four: * {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|ja|櫛明玉神|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto=Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|lt=Kushiakarutama-no-Kami|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}} (also known as Kushiakarutama-no-Mikoto) * {{ill|Ōnamuchi-no-Kami|ja|大名持神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōnamuchi-no-Kami|qq=}} * {{ill|Sukunabikona-no-Kami|ja|少彦名神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sukunabikona-no-Kami|qq=}} * {{ill|Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|ja|五十猛神|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Isotakeru-no-Mikoto|qq=}} == History == The origin of the shrine is unknown. It is mentioned in the {{ill|Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo no Kuni Fudoki|lt=Izumo Fudoki|ja|Izumo Province 風土記|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Izumo Fudoki|qq=}} as "Tamatsukuri-yu Shrine." The shrine has been supported by various ruling clans over the centuries, including the {{ill|Matsue Domain|ja|松江藩|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Matsue Domain|qq=}} during the Edo period. The current main hall was rebuilt in 1857 (Ansei 4), following the Taisha-zukuri architectural style. After the {{ill|Meiji Restoration|ja|明治維新|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Meiji Restoration|qq=}}, the shrine was Ranked as a {{ill|Village Shrine|ja|村社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Village Shrine|qq=}} before being promoted to {{ill|Prefectural Shrine|ja|県社|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Prefectural Shrine|qq=}} in 1928 (Shōwa 3). == Grounds == [[File:Tamatsukuriyu jinja.jpg|thumb|220px|right|{{center|Main Hall}}]] * First Torii Gate - Inscribed by {{ill|Reijirō
